item.title: APT29 Mobile Zero-Click Campaign and Android Critical Vulnerability Patches
item.content:encoded:
Window: 04 Nov 07:00 → 04 Nov 11:00 UTC (4 hours)

Hackers use n-day exploits in zero-click attacks on iOS, Android devices — Must Read

APT29-linked attackers used compromised and spoofed websites to silently profile iOS and Android visitors and deliver device-specific exploit chains that stole cookies, credentials, messaging data, and other sensitive information. Apple and Google have patched the exploited flaws, so users should install the latest available updates.

  • Sekoia attributed a large-scale watering-hole campaign to APT29 with moderate-to-high confidence, targeting iOS and Android users through compromised websites and lookalike domains.
  • Injected JavaScript profiled visitors’ devices and browser versions, after which a command-and-control server delivered platform-specific exploit chains without requiring user interaction.
  • The iOS exploit chains targeted Safari cookies and, on iOS 18.5, could collect WhatsApp and Telegram databases, Keychain credentials, location data, and photos.
  • The Android chain targeted Chrome versions 139 through 145 except 143 and used AndroSnitch to collect Chrome cookies, login data, browsing history, and saved Wi-Fi credentials.
  • Apple and Google have patched the vulnerabilities used in the campaign, and Sekoia said the payloads did not establish persistence, so rebooting ends the malicious activity until the victim revisits a compromised site.

Technologies: browser, mobile-os

Products: ios, android, safari, chrome, plerdy-seo-tracker, whatsapp, telegram

Vendors: apple, google, sekoia, plerdy

Google Issues Patches for Critical Android Flaw That Could Allow RCE Without User Interaction — Must Read

Google’s November 2026 Android security update fixes CVE-2026-58868, a critical heap buffer overflow affecting Android 14–17 that could enable remote code execution without user interaction. Users should install the 2026-11-01 patch level or later, while the 2026-11-05 level includes all November fixes.

  • Google’s November 2026 Android security bulletin fixes CVE-2026-58868, a critical flaw affecting Android 14 through 17 that could allow remote code execution without user interaction.
  • CVE-2026-58868 is an out-of-bounds write caused by a heap buffer overflow in the onOutputReceived function in FrameDecoder.cpp.
  • Android devices need the 2026-11-01 security patch level or later for fixes covering CVE-2026-58868, while the 2026-11-05 patch level covers every flaw in the November bulletin.
  • Another critical flaw, CVE-2026-58882, could allow a remote denial-of-service attack through Android’s WAP Push SMS message code without user interaction.
  • Google’s November bulletin lists 216 vulnerabilities, including 23 rated Critical, and reported no known exploitation as of November 4.

Technologies: mobile-os

Products: android, android-runtime, google-play-system-update

Vendors: google, mediatek, qualcomm, arm, imagination-technologies, unisoc

UK Cybercrime Journal: Beacon CRM Breach Impacts Over 1,500 Charities — Should Read

Beacon CRM exposed database backups for more than 1,000 UK charities after an AWS access key was leaked in public JavaScript artifacts, putting donor and service-user personal data at risk. The incident underscores the supply-chain impact of poor secret management and overly broad cloud access permissions.

  • Beacon CRM reported that attackers used an AWS access key exposed in publicly accessible JavaScript build artifacts to gain access around 27 July 2026.
  • From 27 to 28 July 2026, the attackers downloaded full database backups containing records from more than 1,000 UK charity customers.
  • The affected backups included names, email addresses, phone numbers, home addresses, donation histories, and uploaded attachments, but did not contain payment card numbers or live bank details.
  • Beacon CRM detected the unauthorised activity on 29 July, revoked the exposed credentials, and began notifying affected organisations between 30 July and 3 August.
  • The article states that some stored backups contained historical records and data that individuals had previously requested be deleted.

Technologies: cloud-platform, backup, database, iam

Products: beacon-crm, amazon-web-services

Vendors: beacon, amazon-web-services

Russian Police Arrest 3 Suspected VasyGrek Hackers, Dismantle Criminal Infrastructure — Should Read

Russian police arrested three suspected members of the financially motivated VasyGrek (Fluffy Wolf) hacking group and dismantled infrastructure used to phish organizations and steal funds. The group has targeted organizations across Russia, Belarus, and Kazakhstan using phishing-delivered malware and remote-access tools.

  • Russian authorities arrested three suspected VasyGrek members, searched their residences and offices, and seized computers, communication devices, and other evidence.
  • The Russian Interior Ministry said the group is suspected of stealing funds from organizational accounts and creating, distributing, and using malicious software.
  • In a September 2025 case, attackers allegedly sent a fake business email carrying a supposed reconciliation report, leading to the theft of 660,000 rubles from an unnamed organization.
  • Kaspersky recorded more than 100 attempted VasyGrek attacks against organizations in Russia, Belarus, and Kazakhstan between January and September 2026.
  • The group primarily targeted metallurgical organizations, wholesale suppliers, and government agencies, while healthcare, oil and gas, energy, finance, and agriculture organizations were also affected.

Technologies: remote-access

Vendors: kaspersky, bi-zone, f6

item.title: cPGuard Supply-Chain Breach, Binance Heist, and X.CPE Botnet Disruption
item.content:encoded:
Window: 03 Nov 19:00 → 03 Nov 23:00 UTC (4 hours)

Binance says fake job interview led to $6.3 billion crypto heist — Must Read

Binance says North Korean Lazarus/TraderTraitor hackers stole about $6.34 billion after luring an engineer through a fake job interview into running malware that compromised wallet infrastructure. The exchange has rebuilt affected systems and says roughly $2.85 billion was frozen or intercepted.

  • Binance said North Korean hackers stole about $6.34 billion in digital assets after compromising its wallet infrastructure.
  • The intrusion began when a Binance software engineer was deceived by a fake recruiter and downloaded a coding assignment containing previously unseen malware.
  • Binance said the malware replaced the legitimate Homebrew pyenv executable on the engineer’s Mac to run commands from an attacker-controlled server.
  • By October 20, the attackers had used the compromised engineer’s computer and an internal AI tool to compromise two additional wallet-infrastructure employees and obtain credentials and a container deployment token.
  • Binance said it rebuilt affected systems, replaced compromised devices, revoked stolen credentials, and that about $2.85 billion of stolen assets had been frozen or intercepted as of November 3.

Products: binance-exchange, homebrew, pyenv

Vendors: binance, homebrew, pyenv

Hackers hijack cPGuard autoupdate to deploy backdoor, steal data — Should Read

Attackers hijacked OpsShield’s cPGuard update channel using compromised credentials, distributing a backdoor and data-stealing script to nearly 3,000 Linux servers. Administrators should update to cPGuard 5.88.25 or later and immediately rotate passwords, database credentials, cloud secrets, and SSH keys.

  • An attacker used compromised credentials to access OpsShield’s cPGuard update distribution infrastructure on November 2, 2026, and distributed a malicious script through the update channel.
  • The compromised cPGuard versions were 5.88.12 through 5.88.19, and OpsShield said it stopped the malicious distribution within 12 hours.
  • The malicious script targeted Linux password hashes, root database configuration, root shell history, and root SSH authorization and known-host files.
  • OpsShield said the stolen data was uploaded through a compromised account to its licensing server, and its investigation indicated the threat actor retrieved 32 files from each customer.
  • OpsShield said 2,946 servers were affected and advised administrators to update to cPGuard 5.88.25 or later and rotate potentially exposed credentials.

Technologies: firewall, antivirus

Products: cpguard

Vendors: opsshield

Google dismantles massive botnet hidden in Android TV boxes — Should Read

Google, Japanese law enforcement, and cybersecurity firms disrupted the X.CPE botnet, which was preinstalled in more than 1.3 million Android TV boxes and other IoT devices allegedly tied to Chinese OEM Videostrong. The malware turned devices into residential proxies and enabled ad fraud, data theft, and installation of additional payloads.

  • Google, Japanese law enforcement, and cybersecurity firms disrupted the X.CPE botnet, which affected more than 1.3 million devices in over 200 countries.
  • Google linked the operation to Chinese Android OEM Videostrong Technology and said it cut ties with the company and barred it from making devices with preloaded Google apps.
  • Most affected devices were Android TV set-top boxes, though telehealth devices, karaoke machines, and digital signage devices were also found infected.
  • Google said the preinstalled software enabled a residential proxy network, allowing criminal affiliates to resell bandwidth, conduct ad fraud, steal data, deliver video content, and install additional software.
  • Google said it took legal action to disrupt domains used to control the botnet, which it said effectively rendered the malware benign by severing its communications.

Technologies: mobile-os, iot-device, proxy

Products: android, android-tv

Vendors: google, videostrong-technology

WorkOS says attacker used ARTEX AI to breach internal sales app — Should Read

WorkOS says an attacker used the ARTEX AI offensive-security framework to breach an internal sales application, exposing business contacts, customer account histories, and communication summaries. The company says production services and WorkOS app data were not accessed, and the incident has been contained.

  • WorkOS identified unauthorized access on October 30, 2026, to an internal application used by its sales team.
  • The attacker accessed business contact details, customer account histories, and summaries or excerpts of sales calls, support discussions, and customer Slack conversations.
  • WorkOS said no WorkOS application data or production services were accessed or affected.
  • WorkOS said the attacker used an AI-powered offensive-security framework to automate reconnaissance and exploitation attempts, and founder Michael Grinich identified ARTEX AI as the likely tool.
  • WorkOS disabled external access to the affected application, engaged an independent incident-response firm, and said it would notify affected customers directly.

Products: artex-ai

Vendors: workos

item.title: Gorbag Espionage, Linux CVE-2026-98432, and 3AM Ransomware Dominate Security Updates
item.content:encoded:
Window: 03 Nov 11:00 → 03 Nov 15:00 UTC (4 hours)

Red Hat Patches 9.8-Rated Linux TCP RCE Flaw While Ubuntu Releases Fixes for Testing — Should Read

Red Hat has released critical kernel updates for CVE-2026-98432, a 9.8-rated remotely reachable Linux IPv4 TCP use-after-free flaw that could enable unauthenticated remote code execution. Ubuntu fixes are currently limited to its opt-in -proposed channel, so affected systems should patch and reboot promptly or consider Red Hat’s limited nftables mitigation.

  • CVE-2026-98432 is a Linux kernel IPv4 TCP use-after-free flaw rated 9.8 out of 10 that a remote, unauthenticated attacker can reach and potentially use for remote code execution.
  • Red Hat released fixed kernels for RHEL 8, 9, and 10 on November 1, and systems require a reboot after the updates are installed.
  • Ubuntu has placed fixes for Ubuntu 22.04 LTS, 24.04 LTS, and 26.04 LTS in its opt-in -proposed testing channel, while Ubuntu 20.04, 18.04, and 16.04 did not yet have fixes.
  • The flaw can be triggered by specially crafted IPv4 TCP connection requests using Record Route or Timestamp options sent to a listening TCP port.
  • No vendor, CERT, or the Linux kernel CVE team had reported active exploitation, although Anthropic said an internal research model produced a remote root exploit for Linux servers with an MPTCP listener.

Technologies: operating-system

Products: linux-kernel, red-hat-enterprise-linux, ubuntu, amazon-linux, debian, oracle-linux

Vendors: red-hat, canonical, linux-kernel-project, amazon, debian-project, oracle, suse, anthropic

Russia-Aligned Gorbag Hackers Exploit WinRAR Flaw to Deploy Data-Stealing Malware — Should Read

Russia-aligned Gorbag is targeting Ukrainian government, law-enforcement, and defense entities with phishing lures and the WinRAR flaw CVE-2025-8088 to deploy GIFTEDCROOK and BeautyStealer, stealing browser data, VPN configurations, and sensitive documents.

  • Russia-aligned Gorbag has targeted Ukrainian law-enforcement and justice entities, local administrations near the front line, and the defense sector since at least February 2025.
  • Gorbag uses phishing emails with official- or government-themed lures, including administrative fines and taxes, to deliver malicious attachments.
  • The group deploys GIFTEDCROOK and BeautyStealer to collect browser data, VPN configurations, and documents of interest from compromised systems.
  • Trend Micro attributed Gorbag to attacks that exploited the patched WinRAR vulnerability CVE-2025-8088 to execute GIFTEDCROOK through a DLL sideloading chain.
  • BeautyStealer can send collected data to an attacker-controlled Telegram chat or a custom FastAPI command-and-control server and then remove itself from the affected device.

Technologies: browser

Products: winrar, google-chrome, microsoft-edge, mozilla-firefox, opera

Vendors: eset, rarlab, google, microsoft, mozilla, opera

Russia dismantles infrastructure of VasyGrek cybercrime group, detains three suspects — Should Read

Russian police dismantled infrastructure tied to the VasyGrek (Fluffy Wolf) cybercrime group and detained three suspects accused of phishing-driven theft and malware distribution. The group had targeted organizations across Russia, Belarus, and Kazakhstan, with Kaspersky detecting more than 100 attempted attacks in 2026.

  • Russian authorities said they dismantled infrastructure used by the VasyGrek, also known as Fluffy Wolf, cybercrime group and detained three suspected members.
  • The suspected leader was placed under house arrest, while two alleged accomplices were released under travel restrictions.
  • Authorities said the group used phishing websites impersonating financial and accounting services and remotely accessed victims' computers using tools purchased on dark web marketplaces.
  • In a September 2025 incident described by investigators, attackers allegedly transferred more than 660,000 rubles from an unnamed company's online banking system after an accounting employee opened a malicious email attachment.
  • Kaspersky reported detecting more than 100 attempted VasyGrek attacks from January through September 2026 against organizations in Russia, Belarus, and Kazakhstan.

Technologies: remote-access

Vendors: kaspersky

UK school estate hit by 3AM ransomware in suspected AI-assisted attack — Should Read

A 3AM ransomware affiliate encrypted about 37 systems at a UK school estate after moving laterally from an unmanaged host, stealing credentials and financial data, and linking separate Active Directory domains. Bitdefender says the attacker’s repeated, incrementally altered commands may indicate use of an AI-assisted agentic workflow, though it could not verify the tooling.

  • A 3AM ransomware affiliate encrypted about 37 of nearly 50 machines it reached at a UK school estate after accessing the environment from an unmanaged host.
  • Bitdefender observed repeated commands that were slightly modified at 40- to 100-second intervals, a pattern it said resembled an automated AI agent loop, but it could not verify whether or how a language model was used.
  • The attacker extracted credentials from three Veeam backup servers, copied a Chrome credentials database, and used Mimikatz and LSASS memory-dumping tools.
  • The attacker created two backdoor domain administrator accounts, configured two-way trusts across three previously separate Active Directory domains, and stole financial data.
  • The attackers attempted to disable Sophos and Bitdefender protections, delete system-state backups, and deploy 3AM's Rust-based encryptor; encryption succeeded on about 37 systems.

Technologies: browser, backup

Products: google-chrome

Vendors: bitdefender, veeam, sophos, google

Police seizes over 100 servers in investment scam crackdown — Should Read

European law enforcement arrested seven suspects and seized more than 100 servers linked to a crime-as-a-service operation that supplied fraudulent investment platforms to scam call centers targeting victims in at least 50 countries.

  • European law enforcement authorities arrested seven suspects and seized more than 100 servers in an operation targeting a company suspected of providing fraudulent trading websites to criminal groups.
  • The investigation involved authorities from Albania, Cyprus, Finland, Germany, Kosovo, and North Macedonia, with support from Europol and Eurojust.
  • The case began after a German couple reported they could not withdraw funds invested through an online trading platform, and investigators linked call-center operators to potential victims in at least 50 countries.
  • The scam used deceptive advertisements and fake online account profits to persuade victims to make increasingly large transfers, then delayed or blocked withdrawals.
  • Investigators said evidence indicated the company operated a crime-as-a-service model from Cyprus and Israel and supplied clients running fraudulent call centers in Albania, Kosovo, and North Macedonia.

Free the Model, Sell the Gateway: Prompt Adware hidden in Jailbreak Bundles — May Read

Check Point Research found that the Haiou Codex jailbreak bundle persistently modifies agent prompts to bypass safety guardrails and inject advertisements for its creator’s LLM gateway, making it a form of prompt adware. The dual-use package was also found alongside tools used by a cybercrime actor, highlighting supply-chain and misuse risks from untrusted AI-agent configuration bundles.

  • Check Point Research analyzed Haiou, a jailbreak bundle for OpenAI Codex that uses prompts and security-focused skills intended to weaken model safeguards for hacking, software cracking, and information-security tasks.
  • Haiou modifies Codex global instruction files to make the agent display an advertisement for the zz.aiapi2025.top LLM gateway in response to specified greetings and activation words.
  • The Haiou payload is packaged in encrypted archives that its launcher verifies and decrypts before installing modular prompt files and six skills related to penetration testing, reverse engineering, license cracking, and game security.
  • Researchers found Haiou on a misconfigured server associated with a threat actor that also hosted Cobalt Strike, VulnClaw, and the Ladon framework, although the article states there is no evidence linking Haiou’s author to cybercrime.
  • The bundle includes an uninstaller that restores the original configurations and removes the injected advertisement.

Technologies: api-gateway, source-control

Products: openai-codex, claude-code, haiou, cobalt-strike, vulnclaw, ladon, codex-x, zz-aiapi2025-top

Vendors: openai, github

Google adds new $250,000 Cloud VRP reward for Root-in-Cloud bugs — May Read

Google has added a $250,000 top-tier Cloud VRP reward for researchers who safely demonstrate unauthorized full administrative control of arbitrary Google Cloud organizations or projects without prior access. The program targets severe tenant-isolation and cross-service flaws, with strict rules preventing testing against real customer environments.

  • Google has introduced a $250,000 top-tier reward in its Cloud Vulnerability Reward Program for qualifying Root-in-Cloud vulnerabilities.
  • Qualifying reports must demonstrate unauthorized full administrative control of arbitrary Google Cloud organizations or projects without prior access or special project setup.
  • The reward covers issues such as tenant-isolation bypasses and cross-service logic flaws, and Google will evaluate certain production-infrastructure code-execution findings for Root-in-Cloud eligibility.
  • Researchers cannot qualify if their exploit requires compromised credentials, social engineering, user interaction, or prior access to the target project.
  • Google requires researchers to use a designated service account to safely prove unauthorized access rather than testing exploits against real customer projects.

Technologies: cloud-platform, iam

Products: google-cloud, google-cloud-vulnerability-reward-program, borg, google-cloud-iam

Vendors: google

How to win your own bot detection benchmark — Optional

The article argues that Proof of Human’s 99% bot-detection benchmark is too narrow because it tests only a small set of automated sessions and ignores false positives, real-traffic context, distributed attacks, and adversarial bypass techniques. Organizations should evaluate anti-bot tools on their own production traffic and against realistic, evolving attacker behavior rather than relying on leaderboard-style detection percentages.

  • Proof of Human’s benchmark had five AI agents complete a five-question survey 20 times each, producing up to 100 automated sessions per detection system.
  • The benchmark measured detection of automated sessions but did not evaluate false positives among human respondents, a limitation acknowledged by Proof of Human.
  • The article argues that bot detection in real deployments depends on historical, application, account, and cross-session context that a new survey site with little legitimate traffic does not exercise.
  • The tested automated browsers loaded the anti-bot client, sent expected telemetry, and interacted with the survey, while real attackers may instead replay or forge telemetry, call backend APIs directly, or seek less-protected paths.
  • The article recommends evaluating anti-bot products on real traffic in monitoring mode, investigating false positives, simulating distributed and changing attacks, and assessing resilience to reverse engineering and protocol replay.

Technologies: browser

Products: proof-of-human, recaptcha, hcaptcha, cloudflare-turnstile, cloudflare-bot-management, playwright, comet, grok

Vendors: proof-of-human, google, hcaptcha, cloudflare, castle, microsoft, xai

The cryptography behind electronic voting (and why paper ballots are still essential) — Optional

Cryptography can improve election transparency through encrypted ballots and end-to-end verifiability, but it cannot by itself guarantee secure, private, coercion-free online voting. Paper ballots remain essential because they provide independent physical evidence and constrain the impact of scalable software failures.

  • The article states that electronic ballot return should not be used in general elections because no known technology guarantees the secrecy, security, and verifiability of a marked ballot transmitted over the Internet.
  • Helios and ElectionGuard use encryption and distributed control of decryption keys so that election officials can decrypt a final tally without necessarily revealing individual votes.
  • These systems can use voter challenges and public election records to help detect altered, dropped, or incorrectly recorded encrypted ballots.
  • Electronic voting systems can have scalable failure modes, where a supply-chain or zero-day flaw could affect many voting machines and jurisdictions at once.
  • Paper ballots remain essential because they provide independently auditable physical records and help make software-caused changes to election outcomes detectable.

Products: helios, electionguard

Vendors: microsoft

Malicious Files: Find What Supply Chain Attacks Leave Behind in Your GitHub Repositories and on Developer Machines — Optional

StepSecurity has launched Malicious Files for GitHub in beta and expanded Dev Machine Guard to detect campaign-linked files across repository history and developer endpoints. The tools target planted IDE configurations, malicious workflows, and altered source files associated with supply-chain campaigns such as Miasma, ForceMemo, Megalodon, and GhostAction.

  • StepSecurity launched Malicious Files for GitHub in beta to scan the full history of repositories across branches, pull requests, and tags for files associated with known campaigns.
  • The service uses campaign-specific rules that combine file-path and content checks, and it provides findings showing affected references, introducing commits, matching checks, and matched file versions.
  • Recent campaigns cited in the article used editor settings, altered existing code files, and injected GitHub Actions workflows to trigger credential-stealing or other malicious activity.
  • Dev Machine Guard renamed its Suspicious Files feature to Malicious Files and added a Rules page for viewing, deactivating, and reactivating detection rules across enrolled devices.
  • The article states that organizations should investigate both repositories and developer machines, remove malicious files from all locations, and rotate credentials for affected accounts and devices.

Technologies: source-control, ci-cd, edr

Products: malicious-files-for-github, dev-machine-guard, github, github-actions, claude-code, gemini-cli, visual-studio-code, cursor

Vendors: stepsecurity, github, microsoft, anthropic, google

Introducing Zero Wire, a hub for investigating critical Internet vulnerabilities — Optional

Cloudflare launched Zero Wire, a public Cloudflare Radar feed that consolidates critical Internet-facing vulnerability information into actionable briefings with remediation guidance, evidence, and relevant mitigations. It is intended to help security teams rapidly assess exposure and prioritize response to major disclosures.

  • Cloudflare introduced Zero Wire, a public vulnerability intelligence feed on Cloudflare Radar for significant vulnerabilities in Internet-facing software.
  • Each Zero Wire briefing provides a plain-language overview, teams that should investigate, recommended actions, and links to vendor guidance and other supporting evidence.
  • Zero Wire prioritizes critical CVEs and related issues affecting web applications, their runtimes and libraries, and exposed Internet services, rather than cataloging every CVE.
  • The feed separates entries into “Needs attention” for issues requiring active assessment or action and “Reference” for briefings whose guidance has stabilized.
  • Zero Wire can identify available Cloudflare WAF mitigations, but the article states that WAF protections are compensating controls and do not replace vendor-recommended software remediation.

Technologies: waf, cms

Products: zero-wire, cloudflare-radar, cloudflare-waf, php, wordpress, magento

Vendors: cloudflare, php, wordpress, magento, cisa

The 4 Elements of Exposure Prioritization and How to Operationalize Them — Optional

The article argues that organizations should prioritize exposures using threat intelligence, asset criticality, exploitability modeling, and validation of deployed security controls rather than CVSS severity alone. It promotes Picus as a platform for continuously validating which vulnerabilities are genuinely exploitable and business-relevant.

  • The article argues that CVSS severity scores alone do not reliably predict whether a vulnerability will be exploited or what business impact it will have.
  • It presents four elements for exposure prioritization: threat intelligence, asset context and business criticality, exploitability modeling, and security control validation.
  • Threat intelligence can show which exposures attackers are actually exploiting, while exploitability models such as EPSS estimate the likelihood that a vulnerability will be exploited.
  • Security control validation tests whether an exposure can realistically be exploited in a specific organization despite defenses such as segmentation, endpoint protection, detection coverage, and identity controls.
  • The article promotes the Picus Platform as a way to combine these inputs into a continuous Discover, Validate, Prioritize, and Mobilize workflow.

Products: picus-platform, picus-breach-and-attack-simulation, picus-autonomous-penetration-testing, picus-exposure-validation

Vendors: picus-security, gartner

item.title: Synology DSM Ransomware, BTCPay Hot-Wallet Theft, and European Refrigeration Attacks
item.content:encoded:
Window: 03 Nov 07:00 → 03 Nov 11:00 UTC (4 hours)

Synology NAS Devices Targeted in Ransomware Attacks Exploiting Patched DSM Flaw — Must Read

Synology warns that attackers are exploiting an already patched DSM flaw to deploy C3RB3R ransomware on NAS devices running outdated software. Users should immediately update DSM to the fixed version for their release and enable automatic updates.

  • Synology says threat actors are exploiting a DSM vulnerability patched in December 2024 to target NAS devices running outdated software.
  • The attacks encrypt data and demand a ransom, and customer reports identify the ransomware as C3RB3R, which appends the .L0CK3D extension to files.
  • Synology linked the attacks to an advisory covering CVE-2024-10441, CVE-2024-50629, and CVE-2024-10445.
  • CVE-2024-10441 has a CVSS score of 9.8 and can enable remote code execution in DSM's system plugin daemon through unspecified vectors.
  • Synology urges users to update DSM to fixed releases and enable automatic updates.

Technologies: nas, operating-system

Products: diskstation-manager

Vendors: synology, qnap

Hackers Exploit BTCPay Server Flaw to Steal Bitcoin and Litecoin From Hot Wallets — Must Read

Attackers are draining Bitcoin and Litecoin hot wallets from BTCPay Server instances running version 2.4.1 or earlier by exploiting a flaw patched in 2.4.2. Users should upgrade to 2.4.7 and treat affected servers and their wallet secrets as compromised, migrating to a fresh server and new wallet.

  • Attackers stole Bitcoin and Litecoin from hot wallets on BTCPay Server instances running version 2.4.1 or earlier.
  • BTCPay Server said the attackers used a different method to exploit the vulnerability fixed in version 2.4.2, released on August 7, 2026.
  • BTCPay Server recommends that users of version 2.4.1 or earlier move to a fresh server with a new wallet and treat the machine and all stored secrets as compromised.
  • BTCPay Server said it has received no credible reports of hot-wallet drains from users running version 2.4.7.
  • Mercado Bitcoin temporarily paused deposits and withdrawals after a security breach that it said involved approximately $38 million in assets, with $11 million already blocked.

Products: btcpay-server, lnd, trezor-safe-5, binance, polymarket, debugbear

Vendors: btcpay-server, trezor, mercado-bitcoin, binance, polymarket, debugbear, tether

New Wave of Refrigeration Cyberattacks Hits Supermarkets Across Europe, Forcing Stores to Pull Food — Should Read

Cyberattacks on internet-connected refrigeration controllers disrupted supermarkets and small food retailers across several European countries, causing some stores to remove or discard chilled and frozen goods. The incidents appear to target outdated, internet-exposed Danfoss and possibly Copeland systems with default credentials or unpatched software, prompting calls to isolate controllers and use secure remote access.

  • Attackers remotely changed refrigeration settings at supermarkets and food retailers in multiple European countries, warming fridges and freezers and prompting some businesses to remove or discard food.
  • Belgian, Swedish, Estonian, Irish, Dutch, Finnish, Portuguese, and Italian businesses reported affected refrigeration systems, although the reported number of stores and impact varied by company.
  • Several affected systems were made by Danfoss, while a Belgian butcher reported that Copeland equipment was also targeted; some incidents involved older systems, outdated software, internet exposure, or default passwords.
  • No group had claimed responsibility, and authorities had not determined whether the incidents were linked to the earlier attacks on French supermarkets.
  • CERT-FR advised operators to remove affected refrigeration controllers from direct internet access, review configurations and defrost schedules, use secure remote connections, change default passwords, and update firmware.

Technologies: ics-scada, iot-device

Products: ak-sm, ak-sc, ak-sm-800, ak-sc-355, xweb, dixell-xweb

Vendors: danfoss, copeland

MLEP in KICS for Networks 5.0: how machine learning helps track network behavior of OT devices — Optional

Kaspersky Industrial CyberSecurity for Networks 5.0 introduces MLEP, a machine-learning component that analyzes industrial network behavior to improve OT asset categorization and flag deviations such as new hosts, protocols, scanning activity, unusual transfer volumes, and atypical operating times.

  • Kaspersky Industrial CyberSecurity for Networks 5.0 includes the Machine Learning Event Processor (MLEP), which can refine industrial device categories and detect unusual network behavior.
  • MLEP represents network sessions as 15-second event fragments containing endpoint, port, direction, protocol, packet-count, and packet-size information rather than storing every packet separately.
  • MLEP can use similar recurring communication patterns among known and uncategorized assets to suggest a category for devices whose roles are not identified directly.
  • The initial MLEP release includes six preconfigured anomaly monitors for new external hosts, new destination-address-and-port combinations, unusually large outbound data volumes, atypical activity times, new protocols, and activity resembling scanning.
  • MLEP alerts are intended to help analysts correlate behavior changes with other events and reconstruct activity around an already detected incident.

Technologies: ics-scada, network-monitoring

Products: kaspersky-industrial-cybersecurity-for-networks, machine-learning-event-processor

Vendors: kaspersky

Health-ISAC’s November 2026 newsletter highlights upcoming regional summits, new sector reports and white papers, an exercise after-action report, community resources, and November events.

item.title: Active Exploitation Targets Siemens IoT2050 and CryptoPayment Gateway CVEs
item.content:encoded:
Window: 03 Nov 03:00 → 03 Nov 07:00 UTC (4 hours)

Attackers Exploit Critical Siemens IoT2050 Flaw to Plant Remote Command Backdoors — Must Read

Attackers are actively exploiting CVE-2026-58115, a critical unauthenticated Node-RED flaw in Siemens SIMATIC IoT2050 Advanced devices, to deploy malicious flows that download malware or create persistent remote command backdoors. Organizations should update to version 4.3.4.1 or later or remove and properly secure Node-RED.

Administrators should update to cPGuard 5.88.25 or later and immediately rotate passwords, database credentials, cloud secrets, and SSH keys.

Google, Japanese law enforcement, and cybersecurity firms disrupted the X.CPE botnet, which was preinstalled in more than 1.3 million Android TV boxes and other IoT devices allegedly tied to Chinese OEM Videostrong. The malware turned devices into residential proxies and enabled ad fraud, data theft, and installation of additional payloads.

  • Google, Japanese law enforcement, and cybersecurity firms disrupted the X.CPE botnet, which affected more than 1.3 million devices in over 200 countries.

Harvard’s November 2025 breach of its alumni and fundraising systems exposed personal data tied to roughly 851,000 email addresses after ShinyHunters allegedly stole and leaked donor, alumni, staff, faculty, and student records.

Composer 2.11 introduces optional dependency cooldowns that delay newly published package versions from being installed, reducing exposure to malicious supply-chain releases.   • Composer 2.11 adds an optional dependency cooldown policy that delays eligibility of newly published package versions during dependency resolution.

The SharePoint Invoice That Was a Form Pointing to Evernote — May Read

A phishing email impersonated a Microsoft 365 file-share invite and routed a law-firm partner through a Microsoft Form posing as a SharePoint invoice to an Evernote link posing as a PDF. The key warning signs were mismatched hosts and contradictory branding, despite the links using legitimate services and passing reputation scans.

  • A founding partner at a U.S. plaintiff-side litigation law firm received a hand-built email impersonating a Microsoft 365 file-sharing invitation.
  • All clickable email elements led to a Microsoft Form styled as a SharePoint overdue invoice, which then linked to an Evernote shared note presented as a PDF.
  • The Microsoft Forms and Evernote links scanned clean, but the claimed SharePoint invoice was hosted on a Forms address and the supposed PDF opened through Evernote.
  • The email contained conflicting identities, including an industrial company in the subject, an unrelated consumer brand in the file name, Google-style language in the HTML title, and a Microsoft-style layout.
  • The recipient reported the message as suspicious, and a human analyst confirmed it was malicious.

Technologies: cloud-platform, email-security

Products: microsoft-forms, sharepoint, microsoft-365, evernote, themis

Vendors: microsoft, evernote, ironscales, nifty

Hardening GitHub Actions Against Outside Threats — Optional

GitHub Actions supply-chain compromises often stem from untrusted code or mutable dependencies reaching privileged release workflows, allowing attackers to steal credentials or ship malicious packages. Defend pipelines by SHA-pinning actions, minimizing token and secret access, separating untrusted builds from publishing, constraining caches and dependency installs, and isolating runners and network egress.

  • Attackers have compromised legitimate software releases by abusing GitHub Actions workflows, third-party actions, dependency installation, caches, and release credentials, causing malicious code to be distributed under trusted package names.
  • GitHub Actions should reference third-party actions by full 40-character commit SHA values rather than mutable tags or branches, while reviewers should also verify that pinned commits genuinely belong to the referenced repository.
  • Workflows should deny GitHub token permissions by default, grant only the minimum permissions to individual jobs, and avoid exposing credentials to jobs that do not need them.
  • Untrusted pull request code should run only in ordinary pull_request workflows without secrets, while privileged follow-up tasks should use artifacts as untrusted data and never check out or execute the pull request’s code.
  • Release pipelines should use deterministic dependency installs, disable lifecycle scripts by default, separate building from publishing, avoid shared cache writes from low-trust workflows, and use isolated ephemeral runners where self-hosted runners are unavoidable.

Technologies: ci-cd, source-control, package-registry, cloud-platform

Products: github-actions, github-actions-cache, github-hosted-runners, dependabot, npm, zizmor, actionlint

Vendors: github, npm, zizmorcore

UK faces ‘unprecedented rise’ in cyberattacks in coming months, warns cyber chief — Optional

The UK’s NCSC warns that AI will soon enable attackers to find and exploit long-neglected weaknesses at unprecedented scale, potentially driving a sharp rise in cyber incidents. The government is responding with AI-based initiatives including Project DROMOS, the NERV Centre, and Cyber Shield to identify and block threats.

  • NCSC chief executive Richard Horne will warn that the UK faces a real prospect of an unprecedented rise in cyber incidents in the coming months as AI enables vulnerabilities to be found and exploited at far greater scale.
  • The NCSC says AI did not create existing security weaknesses, but is exposing years of technical debt and failures to implement basic protections, including unpatched internet-facing applications.
  • The agency assesses that AI-powered malware is highly likely to be used in a ransomware attack on UK critical infrastructure by 2028, and that China and Russia will routinely use AI in cyber operations by then.
  • The UK government has tested frontier AI systems through Project DROMOS, which found hundreds of potential security issues, including critical vulnerabilities, in live government environments.
  • The NCSC plans to fund the £70 million NERV Centre and the first £60 million phase of Cyber Shield to use AI for identifying weaknesses and detecting and blocking attacks across the UK.

Technologies: operating-system

Products: project-dromos, nerv-centre, cyber-shield, linux-kernel

Vendors: national-cyber-security-centre, linux-kernel-project

How to win your own bot detection benchmark — Optional

The article argues that Proof of Human’s 99% bot-detection benchmark is too narrow because it tests only a small set of automated sessions and ignores false positives, real-traffic context, distributed attacks, and adversarial bypass techniques. Organizations should evaluate anti-bot tools on their own production traffic and against realistic, evolving attacker behavior rather than relying on leaderboard-style detection percentages.

  • Proof of Human’s benchmark had five AI agents complete a five-question survey 20 times each, producing up to 100 automated sessions per detection system.
  • The benchmark measured detection of automated sessions but did not evaluate false positives among human respondents, a limitation acknowledged by Proof of Human.
  • The article argues that bot detection in real deployments depends on historical, application, account, and cross-session context that a new survey site with little legitimate traffic does not exercise.
  • The tested automated browsers loaded the anti-bot client, sent expected telemetry, and interacted with the survey, while real attackers may instead replay or forge telemetry, call backend APIs directly, or seek less-protected paths.
  • The article recommends evaluating anti-bot products on real traffic in monitoring mode, investigating false positives, simulating distributed and changing attacks, and assessing resilience to reverse engineering and protocol replay.

The cryptography behind electronic voting (and why paper ballots are still essential) — Optional

Cryptography can improve election transparency through encrypted ballots and end-to-end verifiability, but it cannot by itself guarantee secure, private, coercion-free online voting. Paper ballots remain essential because they provide independent physical evidence and constrain the impact of scalable software failures.

  • The article states that electronic ballot return should not be used in general elections because no known technology guarantees the secrecy, security, and verifiability of a marked ballot transmitted over the Internet.
  • Helios and ElectionGuard use encryption and distributed control of decryption keys so that election officials can decrypt a final tally without necessarily revealing individual votes.
  • These systems can use voter challenges and public election records to help detect altered, dropped, or incorrectly recorded encrypted ballots.
  • Electronic voting systems can have scalable failure modes, where a supply-chain or zero-day flaw could affect many voting machines and jurisdictions at once.
  • Paper ballots remain essential because they provide independently auditable physical records and help make software-caused changes to election outcomes detectable.

StepSecurity has launched Malicious Files for GitHub in beta and expanded Dev Machine Guard to detect campaign-linked files across repository history and developer endpoints. The tools target planted IDE configurations, malicious workflows, and altered source files associated with supply-chain campaigns such as Miasma, ForceMemo, Megalodon, and GhostAction.

  • StepSecurity launched Malicious Files for GitHub in beta to scan the full history of repositories across branches, pull requests, and tags for files associated with known campaigns.
  • The service uses campaign-specific rules that combine file-path and content checks, and it provides findings showing affected references, introducing commits, matching checks, and matched file versions.

  • Dev Machine Guard renamed its Suspicious Files feature to Malicious Files and added a Rules page for viewing, deactivating, and reactivating detection rules across enrolled devices.
  • The article states that organizations should investigate both repositories and developer machines, remove malicious files from all locations, and rotate credentials for affected accounts and devices.

Introducing Zero Wire, a hub for investigating critical Internet vulnerabilities — Optional

Cloudflare launched Zero Wire, a public Cloudflare Radar feed that consolidates critical Internet-facing vulnerability information into actionable briefings with remediation guidance, evidence, and relevant mitigations. It is intended to help security teams rapidly assess exposure and prioritize response to major disclosures.

  • Cloudflare introduced Zero Wire, a public vulnerability intelligence feed on Cloudflare Radar for significant vulnerabilities in Internet-facing software.
  • Each Zero Wire briefing provides a plain-language overview, teams that should investigate, recommended actions, and links to vendor guidance and other supporting evidence.
  • Zero Wire prioritizes critical CVEs and related issues affecting web applications, their runtimes and libraries, and exposed Internet services, rather than cataloging every CVE.
  • The feed separates entries into “Needs attention” for issues requiring active assessment or action and “Reference” for briefings whose guidance has stabilized.
  • Zero Wire can identify available Cloudflare WAF mitigations, but the article states that WAF protections are compensating controls and do not replace vendor-recommended software remediation.

Technologies: waf, cms

Products: zero-wire, cloudflare-radar, cloudflare-waf, php, wordpress, magento

Vendors: cloudflare, php, wordpress, magento, cisa

MLEP in KICS for Networks 5.0: how machine learning helps track network behavior of OT devices — Optional

Kaspersky Industrial CyberSecurity for Networks 5.0 introduces MLEP, a machine-learning component that analyzes industrial network behavior to improve OT asset categorization and flag deviations such as new hosts, protocols, scanning activity, unusual transfer volumes, and atypical operating times.

  • Kaspersky Industrial CyberSecurity for Networks 5.0 includes the Machine Learning Event Processor (MLEP), which can refine industrial device categories and detect unusual network behavior.
  • MLEP represents network sessions as 15-second event fragments containing endpoint, port, direction, protocol, packet-count, and packet-size information rather than storing every packet separately.
  • MLEP can use similar recurring communication patterns among known and uncategorized assets to suggest a category for devices whose roles are not identified directly.
  • The initial MLEP release includes six preconfigured anomaly monitors for new external hosts, new destination-address-and-port combinations, unusually large outbound data volumes, atypical activity times, new protocols, and activity resembling scanning.
  • MLEP alerts are intended to help analysts correlate behavior changes with other events and reconstruct activity around an already detected incident.

Technologies: ics-scada, network-monitoring

Products: kaspersky-industrial-cybersecurity-for-networks, machine-learning-event-processor

Vendors: kaspersky

Monthly Newsletter – November 2026 — Optional

Health-ISAC’s November 2026 newsletter highlights upcoming regional summits and events, new healthcare-sector threat and heartbeat reports, security resources, and published materials including MedTech Security Baselines and the Americas Hobby Exercise after-action report.

Gartner Predicts SOCs Will Have 50% More Engineers Than Analysts by 2028 — Optional

A sponsored Prophet Security article highlights Gartner’s prediction that AI automation will shift SOC work away from alert triage, leaving security operations teams with 50% more engineers than analysts by 2028. It argues SOCs should prepare by emphasizing case ownership, AI-aware detection engineering, threat hunting, and continuous exposure management.

  • Gartner predicts that by 2028, security operations centers will have 50% more engineers than analysts as AI agents take over more alert triage and investigation work.
  • The report recommends that analysts shift from processing alerts to owning cases from start to finish, validating AI findings, choosing responses, and communicating options to those who act on them.
  • Gartner says detection engineering should expand into broader SOC engineering, including prompt design, workflow testing, AI output validation, versioning, testing, and rollback practices.
  • The report advises SOC leaders to measure cases and decisions rather than alert volume, using measures such as case accuracy, cycle time, and decision confidence.
  • Gartner calls continuous threat exposure management a standing SOC function and predicts SOCs will be largely offensively driven by 2030.

Products: prophet-ai

Vendors: prophet-security, gartner

The 4 Elements of Exposure Prioritization and How to Operationalize Them — Optional

Picus argues that vulnerability prioritization should combine threat intelligence, asset criticality, exploitability modeling, and validation of deployed controls rather than relying on CVSS alone. The company promotes its platform as a way to continuously validate which exposures are genuinely exploitable in an organization and prioritize remediation accordingly.

  • The article states that fewer than 10% of vulnerabilities are exploited and argues that CVSS severity scores alone do not predict real-world exploitation or business impact.
  • It presents four inputs for exposure prioritization: threat intelligence, asset context and business criticality, exploitability modeling, and security control validation.
  • Threat intelligence identifies exposures attackers are actively exploiting, while asset context distinguishes risks on critical systems from those on lower-impact assets.
  • Exploit prediction models such as EPSS estimate the likelihood of exploitation but should feed validation rather than serve as a final decision.
  • Picus promotes its platform as combining discovery, validation, prioritization, and mobilization to produce organization-specific exposure ratings.

Chinese hackers use ARTEX AI in automated attacks against 200 orgs — Must Read

Chinese-linked Vapor Panda used the ARTEX AI multi-agent penetration-testing framework, alongside commercial language models, to automate cyberespionage against more than 200 organizations in 14 countries, compromising at least nine. The campaign shows AI agents can conduct reconnaissance, exploitation, credential theft, and lateral activity across multiple intrusions under human supervision.

  • CrowdStrike says the China-linked threat actor Vapor Panda used ARTEX AI in a cyberespionage campaign targeting more than 200 organizations across 14 countries beginning on October 17.
  • The campaign targeted government ministries, telecommunications providers, and organizations in the pharmaceutical, semiconductor, defense, nuclear, and financial sectors, with at least nine organizations compromised.
  • Vapor Panda used DeepSeek and another commercial language model to coordinate AI agents that performed reconnaissance, exploited flaws, deployed remote-control tools, obtained credentials, and pursued alternative paths.
  • In an intrusion against a Greek government entity, the agents forged an administrator token and read mailboxes using authentication keys from a 2022 mail-server directory export.
  • The Dutch Institute for Vulnerability Disclosure said ARTEX AI autonomously reached root-level access on its network in 12 minutes by chaining a Zammad zero-day with a second zero-day that raised its privileges.

Technologies: edr

Products: artex-ai, falcon, zammad

Vendors: crowdstrike, deepseek, zammad

Largest crypto exchange in Brazil confirms cyberattack as millions flow out of platform — Should Read

Mercado Bitcoin, Brazil’s largest crypto exchange, suspended deposits and withdrawals after a cyberattack reportedly drained more than $46 million, though the company says customers were not harmed. Investigators and other crypto platforms have frozen roughly $6.5 million so far, while researchers dispute whether customer wallets were affected.

  • Mercado Bitcoin suspended all deposits and withdrawals following a cybersecurity incident on Monday morning.
  • Blockchain security companies reported that more than $46 million left Mercado Bitcoin late Sunday, although the company did not confirm that amount.
  • Mercado Bitcoin said the incident did not harm customers or cause a data breach, but several blockchain security experts said blockchain records showed funds were taken from some customer wallets.
  • Tether froze approximately $4.5 million linked to the theft, while other platforms froze another $2 million in cryptocurrency.
  • Mercado Bitcoin said it is investigating the incident, tracking the assets, coordinating with authorities, and plans to restore the platform in the coming days.

Products: mercado-bitcoin

Cyberattacks disrupted commercial refrigeration systems at grocery stores across six European countries, reportedly raising temperatures to 50°C and spoiling food. The incidents again appear linked to internet-exposed Danfoss StoreView controllers, though many exposed systems remain unpatched.

  • On November 2, grocers, butchers, and small shops in Belgium, Estonia, Ireland, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, and Sweden reported attacks on commercial refrigeration units.
  • Attackers reportedly raised refrigeration temperatures to 50°C (122°F), causing food to spoil or melt in dozens of stores.
  • Reports indicated that Danfoss StoreView refrigeration controllers, which were involved in attacks on French grocers on October 11, may also have been involved in this wave.
  • Censys observed just over 1,000 internet-exposed Danfoss StoreView instances globally, with France having the highest concentration.
  • Censys found that France had 220 exposed StoreView instances at the time of analysis, down from 1,825 before the October attacks, and 41% of the remaining French instances appeared to run patched firmware.

Google disrupts million-device XCPE Android malware botnet, bans TV box maker — Should Read

Google disrupted the XCPE botnet, which it says was deliberately preinstalled by Chinese Android TV-box maker Videostrong on more than 1.3 million devices and used for ad fraud, residential proxying, and malware delivery. Google revoked Videostrong’s Android TV certification, but affected owners must install clean firmware or disconnect devices because the backdoor persists in the OEM partition.

  • Google and industry partners disrupted the XCPE botnet, which Google says included more than 1.3 million Android TV streaming boxes with malware embedded during manufacturing.
  • Google attributed the botnet with high confidence to Chinese manufacturer Videostrong Technology Co., alleging it intentionally installed a persistent backdoor and sold access to criminal affiliates.
  • The XCPE backdoor could install apps silently, disable Google Play Protect, run system-level commands, capture screenshots, collect device and account information, and create remote access to devices.
  • Google revoked Videostrong’s Android TV license and banned the company and future affiliates from producing certified Android devices or supplying software to certified vendors.
  • Google said affected devices remain infected because the malware can restore itself from the OEM partition, so owners need clean firmware or must disconnect the devices from the internet.

Technologies: mobile-os, iot-device, proxy

Products: android-tv, mecool-km9pro-max

Vendors: google, videostrong-technology, mecool

BTCPay Server warns of hot wallet crypto thefts on outdated instances — Should Read

BTCPay Server says attackers are draining hot wallets on instances running version 2.4.1 or older, apparently by gaining administrator access. Operators should immediately take outdated servers offline and update to version 2.4.7.

  • BTCPay Server warned that attackers have been draining hot wallets on instances running version 2.4.1 or earlier.
  • The project said its investigation identified an attack vector affecting versions released on or before July 23, 2026, and urged users to update to version 2.4.7.
  • BTCPay Server founder Nicolas Dorier said the attacks did not target public servers and investigators were examining how attackers logged in as administrators on versions older than 2.4.2.
  • BTCPay Server began receiving theft reports and asked VPS hosting providers to take affected server instances offline as a precaution.
  • Users who lost funds are asked to contact security@btcpayserver.org and report the losses to local authorities.

Russia’s Rosstat confirmed it suffered a cyberattack after Belarusian Cyber Partisans and Silent Crow claimed they infiltrated its network for months, destroyed infrastructure and stole sensitive state data. Rosstat disputes that protected data or databases were compromised, and the hackers’ broader claims remain unverified.

  • Rosstat confirmed that it was targeted by a cyberattack but said it found no evidence that protected information was leaked or its databases were compromised.
  • Belarusian Cyber Partisans and Silent Crow claimed they had access to Rosstat’s network for months before destroying servers and large-scale storage systems over the weekend.
  • The groups alleged they accessed about 25,000 computers and devices and obtained economic, demographic, personal, census and internal government information, though these claims could not be independently verified.
  • Rosstat collects official Russian population, economic and social statistics and holds demographic records, including information from Russian-occupied Ukrainian territories.
  • The same two groups previously claimed responsibility for a July 2025 cyberattack on Aeroflot that caused more than 100 flight cancellations.

Thoughts on Vulnerability Response in the Era of the Vulnpocalypse and PHP2Shell — Should Read

AI may shorten the path from obscure flaws to working exploits, but the decisive factor in vulnerability response remains whether organizations can identify, own, and safely update their systems. PHP2Shell showed rapid patching by well-maintained environments while millions of older PHP deployments remain difficult or impossible to remediate without migration, backported fixes, or isolation.

  • The article argues that raw vulnerability counts are a poor measure of risk because only a small share of disclosed flaws are observed being exploited in the wild.
  • PHP2Shell involved two critical PHP memory-corruption flaws, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, which could allow unauthenticated remote code execution on PHP web servers under certain conditions.
  • Censys reported that more than 11 million PHP services moved from affected to fixed versions after patches became available on October 21, with most updates occurring during the first few days.
  • As of October 29, more than 30 million PHP services still reported affected versions, including roughly 23 million using PHP 8.1 or older branches without official PHP2Shell fixes.
  • The article concludes that making software easier to upgrade, including through migration paths, compatibility support, and potentially AI-assisted maintenance, is essential for improving vulnerability response.

Polymarket will reimburse $3.9 million to users affected after attackers hijacked a DebugBear performance-monitoring script to drain funds through active sessions. The company says it removed the malicious script, reset sessions, and had fully refunded 95% of affected wallets as of Saturday.

Healthcare’s rapid adoption of AI is expanding the volume of sensitive patient data and increasing exposure to third-party security failures. Health-ISAC highlights a SquareML vendor access-key exposure affecting Denver Health Medical Plan as an example of the growing risk.

  • Phil Englert of Health-ISAC said that increased AI integration affects the amount of sensitive data flowing through healthcare systems.

Healthcare organizations face growing vishing threats from groups such as ShinyHunters, which spoof internal callers and trick staff into divulging credentials and MFA tokens. Strong help-desk identity verification, vishing simulations, and phishing-resistant authentication are key defenses.

  • Health-ISAC and Mandiant warn that financially motivated groups, including ShinyHunters, are increasingly using voice phishing against the healthcare sector.
  • The described tactic includes spoofing an internal phone number, pressuring an employee to visit a fake remote-login page, and capturing credentials and multi-factor authentication tokens.
  • The article says AI can reduce the time needed to research targets and remove language barriers for these campaigns.
  • Errol Weiss and Trevor Horwitz recommend vishing simulations, stronger identity checks for multi-factor authentication resets, and phishing-resistant authentication.

This weekly threat intelligence roundup highlights major breaches, AI-enabled threat activity, and actively exploited vulnerabilities affecting organizations and products including Cisco, Drupal, Node.js, and Linux systems.

Over 1,000 GitLab servers vulnerable to ongoing RCE attacks — Must Read

More than 1,000 internet-exposed GitLab servers remain unpatched against CVE-2026-97229, a maximum-severity unauthenticated RCE flaw that CISA says is actively being exploited. Self-managed GitLab users should immediately upgrade to versions 19.4.2, 19.3.5, or 19.2.8.

  • CVE-2026-97229 is a maximum-severity GitLab flaw that can allow an unauthenticated user to execute arbitrary code through a specially crafted regular expression in a CI/CD configuration.
  • GitLab released patches for CVE-2026-97229 in GitLab CE and EE versions 19.4.2, 19.3.5, and 19.2.8, and said GitLab.com is already patched.
  • CISA confirmed that CVE-2026-97229 is being exploited in the wild and added it to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities Catalog.
  • Shadowserver reported that it tracked more than 1,000 internet-exposed GitLab instances vulnerable to CVE-2026-97229 three weeks after patches became available.
  • Shadowserver also reported more than 11,300 GitLab instances vulnerable to CVE-2026-110264 out of roughly 39,000 GitLab instances it sees daily.

Technologies: ci-cd, source-control

Products: gitlab-ce, gitlab-ee, gitlab-cicd-regular-expression-compiler

Vendors: gitlab

Synology warns of C3RB3R ransomware attacks targeting NAS devices — Must Read

Synology is urging NAS owners to immediately update DiskStation Manager and disable Internet access to its management interface after C3RB3R ransomware attackers began exploiting a vulnerability patched in December 2024 to encrypt data on unpatched devices.

  • Synology warned that C3RB3R ransomware actors are exploiting a vulnerability patched in December 2024 to target NAS devices running outdated DiskStation Manager versions.
  • Synology urged users to update DiskStation Manager immediately, enable automatic updates, and block internet access to the management web interface.
  • The November 2024 advisory linked by Synology describes fixes for CVE-2024-10441, CVE-2024-50629, and CVE-2024-10445, which could allow arbitrary code execution, file reading, or file writing on unpatched devices.
  • Affected users reported that the ransomware adds a .L0CK3D extension to encrypted files and leaves a read-me3.txt ransom note directing victims to purchase a C3rb3r Decryptor.
  • Shadowserver tracks more than 380,000 internet-exposed Synology NAS devices, though it does not report how many are patched or honeypots.

Technologies: nas, operating-system

Products: diskstation-manager

Vendors: synology

Critical Langflow Flaws Could Let Unauthenticated Attackers Run Code on Servers — Should Read

Langflow versions 1.0.0 through 1.12.8 contain critical flaws that can let unauthenticated remote attackers bypass authentication or execute arbitrary code, including through MCP tool enumeration. Organizations should upgrade to Langflow 1.13.0 immediately, as IBM provides no workaround.

  • IBM reported that Langflow versions 1.0.0 through 1.12.8 are affected by four vulnerabilities, including two critical issues rated 9.8.
  • CVE-2026-93680 can allow unauthenticated attackers to bypass authentication, while CVE-2026-110186 can allow unauthenticated arbitrary code execution through Model Context Protocol tool enumeration.
  • A public Metasploit Framework module for CVE-2026-93680 can connect to a Langflow server's MCP endpoint without credentials and list its available tools.
  • Langflow 1.13.0, released October 22, fixes the flaws, turns automatic login off by default, and is the only remediation IBM provides for affected deployments.
  • IBM also published 29 additional Langflow CVE records on October 29, including CVE-2026-104339, an unauthenticated arbitrary-code-execution issue rated 9.8.

Products: langflow, metasploit-framework

Vendors: ibm, langflow, rapid7

Attackers Pose as IT Support on Microsoft Teams, Abuse AD CS to Steal Company Data — Should Read

Attackers impersonated IT support in Microsoft Teams to trick employees into granting Quick Assist access, then abused misconfigured Active Directory Certificate Services to obtain privileged certificates, access domain controllers, and steal data. The incidents underscore that securing AD CS templates and web enrollment, restricting remote-support access, and fully containing compromised identities are critical.

  • Attackers impersonated company IT or help-desk staff in Microsoft Teams and convinced employees to share Quick Assist connection codes, giving the attackers control of their workstations.
  • Microsoft investigated two intrusions in which attackers abused insecure Active Directory Certificate Services configurations to obtain certificates for privileged accounts, including a domain controller.
  • In one case, attackers exploited an ESC1 certificate template weakness, used DCSync against a domain controller, and copied company data from a file server to an external SFTP server using a renamed Rclone tool.
  • In the other case, attackers used PetitPotam and an ESC8 NTLM relay to obtain a domain controller certificate, but Defender alerts and workstation isolation stopped further activity.
  • Microsoft said the activity exploited social engineering and insecure configuration rather than a flaw in Microsoft Teams, and it was not attributed to a known group.

Technologies: remote-access, iam, edr, operating-system

Products: microsoft-teams, quick-assist, active-directory-certificate-services, microsoft-defender-for-endpoint, microsoft-defender-for-identity, windows-server

Vendors: microsoft

DarkBlinders Compromises Israeli Target and Iraqi Kurdish Government Cloud Environment — Should Read

Iran-aligned DarkBlinders targeted a high-profile Israeli individual and a Kurdistan Regional Government cloud environment using tailored phishing, fake software and recruitment lures to deploy ShelbyLoader and ShelbyC2. Researchers assess the activity may be linked to broader Iran-nexus clusters associated with APT34.

  • Dream Research Labs reported that Iran-aligned DarkBlinders compromised a high-profile individual in Israel and a government cloud environment in the Kurdistan Region of Iraq between August and October 2026.
  • DarkBlinders used targeted phishing, lookalike government, webmail, and cloud-service domains, fake recruitment offers, and a counterfeit StarkMeet videoconferencing application to collect credentials or deliver malicious files.
  • The group’s infection chain used a malicious Visual Studio project, AppDomainManager injection, and DLL sideloading to deploy ShelbyLoader V2, ShelbyC2, and the Blackwood tunneling utility.
  • Dream assessed with medium confidence that DarkBlinders activity overlaps operationally with UNC5795 and Dust Specter, with potential links to sub-clusters associated with APT34.
  • Separately, the Iranian government-sponsored Prince of Persia group was observed operating a U.S.-hosted command-and-control server in 2026 after a three-month period of inactivity.

Technologies: source-control

Products: visual-studio, github, telegram

Vendors: microsoft, github, telegram

Hackers disrupt refrigeration systems at European supermarkets — Should Read

A cyberattack remotely altered refrigeration controls at more than 115 supermarkets and shops across several European countries, causing freezers to shut down, defrost, or heat up and leading to product losses. The incidents may exploit the same weakness used in recent attacks on French stores’ refrigeration controllers.

  • A cyberattack disrupted refrigeration and freezer systems at more than 115 stores in Belgium, the Netherlands, Sweden, Luxembourg, Ireland, and Estonia.
  • Affected equipment was reported to have been shut down, switched to defrost mode, or in one case begun generating heat, causing rising temperatures and product losses.
  • The affected chains include ICA, Coop, Ahold Delhaize, Carrefour, Spar Colruyt, Intermarché, SuperValu, and Selver, while additional Dutch butcher shops and neighborhood stores were also impacted.
  • An ICA store manager said temperature settings were changed overnight to 50°C and could not be modified, forcing the store to discard frozen food.
  • Sabcobel director Stephan Moelans said the attacker used the same weakness involved in similar refrigerator attacks in France the previous month, and that remote activation of defrost functions caused the disruption.

Technologies: ics-scada, iot-device

Products: danfoss-ak-sm, danfoss-ak-sc, copeland-dixell-xweb

Vendors: sabcobel, danfoss, copeland, dixell

Apple warns users in 99 countries of mercenary spyware — Should Read

Apple issued mercenary-spyware threat notifications to targeted users in 99 countries, including journalists in Turkey and Lebanon. The alerts are not attributed to a specific actor, but highlight continuing sophisticated surveillance of investigative reporters.

  • Apple sent a new round of threat notifications warning targeted users in 99 countries about suspected mercenary spyware attacks.
  • Recipients who publicly disclosed notifications include Turkey-based Middle East Eye bureau chief Ragıp Soylu and Lebanese journalist and documentary filmmaker Radwan Mortada.
  • Apple said it does not attribute these attacks to particular actors or regions because mercenary spyware campaigns are costly, sophisticated, and global.
  • Mortada said his phone was previously targeted with Pegasus zero-click spyware in 2017 and 2021.
  • Apple had not publicly posted the latest notifications on its website and did not respond to a request for comment.

Products: apple-threat-notifications

Vendors: apple

Russian and Ukrainian hackers hijack emergency apps to spread fake nuclear attack warnings — Should Read

Hackers compromised Ukraine’s Air Alert app and Russia’s EMERCOM emergency app to send false nuclear, radiation, and attack warnings, though both countries said their primary public-warning systems remained unaffected. The incidents highlight how emergency-notification apps can be exploited for wartime disinformation and panic.

  • Ukraine’s Air Alert app was likely compromised, causing Kyiv residents to receive fake notifications about radiation, chemical threats, street fighting, and a possible Oreshnik missile strike.
  • The Air Alert developers disabled push notifications and temporarily suspended the service before gradually restoring basic alerts with additional security measures.
  • A group calling itself DC8044 claimed it accessed Russia’s EMERCOM emergency app and used it to distribute false warnings that nuclear warheads had been launched toward Russia.
  • Russia’s Emergency Situations Ministry acknowledged that its mobile app had been hacked but said its primary public-warning infrastructure, including sirens, loudspeakers, text messages, television, and radio, was unaffected.
  • Ukrainian authorities said the national warning system and Kyiv Digital app remained operational despite the compromise of the Air Alert app.

Products: air-alert, emercom, kyiv-digital

Vendors: ajax-systems, ministry-of-emergency-situations-russia

Microsoft fixes Smart App Control broken by October Windows update — May Read

Microsoft fixed an issue caused by the October 2026 KB5127648 Windows 11 update that left Smart App Control grayed out and unable to be enabled. The fix is available in the KB5127936 preview update, with registry and Group Policy workarounds for organizations that defer it.

  • Microsoft resolved an issue in which the October 2026 KB5127648 Windows 11 security update prevented some users from enabling Smart App Control.
  • The issue affected Windows 11 24H2 and later devices where Smart App Control had been turned off, leaving the option grayed out, while devices with it already enabled remained protected.
  • Microsoft said the fix is included in Windows updates released on October 28, 2026 and later, including the KB5127936 preview update.
  • Organizations that do not want to deploy the preview update can use Microsoft-provided registry commands or Group Policy settings as a temporary workaround.
  • The KB5127936 preview update also addresses Remote Desktop failures tied to Administrator protection and Always On VPN issues triggered by September 2026 cumulative updates.

Technologies: operating-system, antivirus, remote-access, vpn

Products: windows-11, smart-app-control, windows-security, microsoft-defender, smartscreen, remote-desktop, always-on-vpn

Vendors: microsoft

Backporting security fixes at scale with Codex — May Read

Trail of Bits says its Codex-assisted workflow can reduce the human effort to backport security fixes into stable Linux releases from days to hours, helping address thousands of known CVEs that remain unpatched in long-term-supported software. The project has already helped land fixes for 149 CVEs in stable Linux kernel branches and is extending the effort to Fedora and Ubuntu packages.

  • Trail of Bits says its Codex workflow uses agents to identify missing fixes, adapt patches for older code, run tests, assemble validation evidence, and prepare submission packets for human review.
  • The project reports that, by October 29, it helped deliver fixes for 149 distinct CVEs into stable Linux kernel releases and submitted several fixes for Fedora and Ubuntu packages.
  • For a straightforward backport, Trail of Bits estimates that patch preparation and review require about 30 minutes of human attention, while more involved cases can require around three hours.
  • The article reports that supported Linux kernel stable branches had hundreds to thousands of known CVEs fixed in newer branches but still unfixed in the older branch, based on the kernel CVE team’s data as of September 18, 2026.
  • Trail of Bits emphasizes that regression testing and acceptance by package and kernel maintainers remain necessary even when AI reduces the effort required to prepare a backport.

Technologies: operating-system

Is Your SOC Ready for AI Agents? A Maturity Check Before You Deploy — Optional

SOC teams should assess data access, investigation standards, human-approval rules, and baseline metrics before deploying AI agents. The sponsored article positions Prophet Security’s AI SOC platform as a way to automate alert investigations, hunting, and detection engineering while retaining human oversight.

  • Prophet Security’s survey of more than 250 security leaders and practitioners found that 40% of security teams use AI daily, 56% are testing it, and 4% have no adoption plans.
  • The article says AI SOC agents can investigate alerts as they arrive by querying connected security tools and documenting the evidence behind their conclusions.
  • Before deploying an AI agent, the article recommends ensuring it has API access to relevant data sources, readable business context, healthy data pipelines, written investigation standards, and defined approval rules.
  • The article states that 28% of alerts are never investigated and that a thorough investigation takes an average of 75 minutes, according to its cited survey.
  • The article promotes Prophet AI as a platform with agents for alert investigation, threat hunting, and detection engineering, with customer-controlled permissions and human approval as the default for response actions.
